```{python}
#| label: fig-dft-cons
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "The netlist `cons.v`: $y = ab + \\bar{a}c + bc$. The term $bc$ is the consensus of the other two: whenever $b = c = 1$, either $ab$ or $\\bar{a}c$ is 1 as well, so the gate `u_bc` never changes the output."
#| fig-alt: "Gate-level circuit with inputs a, b and c on the left. Input a drives the AND gate u_ab and, through the inverter u_inv, the net a_n, which drives the AND gate u_anc. Input b drives u_ab and the AND gate u_bc. Input c drives u_anc and u_bc. The outputs ab, anc and bc of the three AND gates drive the three inputs of the OR gate u_or, whose output is y_o. The gate u_bc and its output are drawn in orange."
import schemdraw as sd
from schemdraw import logic
from schemdraw import elements as elm
sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

ORANGE = '#d79b00'
S = 1.6   # gate scale: inputs 0.8 apart

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=1, fontsize=11, lw=1.5, bgcolor='white', margin=0.2)
    g_ab = logic.And(inputs=2).scale(S).at((4.4, 2.4)).anchor('in1')
    g_anc = logic.And(inputs=2).scale(S).at((4.4, 0.0)).anchor('in1')
    g_bc = logic.And(inputs=2).scale(S).at((4.4, -2.4)).anchor('in1') \
        .color(ORANGE)
    inv = logic.Not().scale(S).at((1.2, 0.0)).anchor('in1')
    g_or = logic.Or(inputs=3).scale(S).at((9.4, 0.4)).anchor('in1')
    elm.Label().at((g_ab.in1[0] + 1.2, g_ab.in1[1] + 0.75)).label('u_ab')
    elm.Label().at((g_anc.in1[0] + 1.2, g_anc.in1[1] + 0.75)).label('u_anc')
    elm.Label().at((g_bc.in1[0] + 1.2, g_bc.in1[1] + 0.75)).label('u_bc',
                                                                 color=ORANGE)
    elm.Label().at((inv.in1[0] + 0.5, 1.05)).label('u_inv')
    elm.Label().at((g_or.in1[0] + 1.3, g_or.in1[1] + 0.7)).label('u_or')

    # a: to u_ab and through the inverter to u_anc
    elm.Label().at((-0.1, 2.4)).label('a', halign='right')
    elm.Line().at((0, 2.4)).to(g_ab.in1)
    elm.Dot(radius=0.07).at((0.7, 2.4))
    elm.Line().at((0.7, 2.4)).to((0.7, 0.0))
    elm.Line().at((0.7, 0.0)).to(inv.in1)
    elm.Line().at(inv.out).to(g_anc.in1)
    elm.Label().at((inv.out[0] + 0.55, 0.3)).label('a_n')
    # b: to u_ab and u_bc
    elm.Label().at((-0.1, 1.6)).label('b', halign='right')
    elm.Line().at((0, 1.6)).to(g_ab.in2)
    elm.Dot(radius=0.07).at((3.3, 1.6))
    elm.Line().at((3.3, 1.6)).to((3.3, -2.4))
    elm.Line().at((3.3, -2.4)).to(g_bc.in1)
    # c: to u_anc and u_bc
    elm.Label().at((-0.1, -0.8)).label('c', halign='right')
    elm.Line().at((0, -0.8)).to(g_anc.in2)
    elm.Dot(radius=0.07).at((3.8, -0.8))
    elm.Line().at((3.8, -0.8)).to((3.8, -3.2))
    elm.Line().at((3.8, -3.2)).to(g_bc.in2)

    # the three products into the OR gate
    for g, pin, x, name, col in ((g_ab, g_or.in1, 8.4, 'ab', 'black'),
                                 (g_anc, g_or.in2, 8.0, 'anc', 'black'),
                                 (g_bc, g_or.in3, 8.4, 'bc', ORANGE)):
        elm.Line().at(g.out).to((x, g.out[1])).color(col)
        elm.Line().at((x, g.out[1])).to((x, pin[1])).color(col)
        elm.Line().at((x, pin[1])).to(pin).color(col)
        elm.Label().at((g.out[0] + 0.4, g.out[1] + 0.25)).label(name,
                                                                color=col)
    elm.Line().at(g_or.out).to((g_or.out[0] + 1.0, g_or.out[1]))
    elm.Label().at((g_or.out[0] + 1.1, g_or.out[1])).label('y_o',
                                                          halign='left')
```
